dimensions.label: Stage & Hiring Pressure
dimensions.description: Series A-C or comparable growth company actively expanding the engineering team, with clear hiring motion and a newly opened role.

levels.0: No real engineering organization, or a temporary 2-3 person team trying to assemble technical capacity.
levels.1: Idea-stage company or speculative reserved headcount.
levels.2: Pre-revenue seed company with unclear engineering organization.
levels.3: Hiring exists but urgency is unclear, or the company is earlier stage but has revenue.
levels.4: Profitable bootstrapped company expanding the team, or growth-stage company with visible technical hiring need.
levels.5: Series A-C or comparable growth company actively expanding the engineering team, with clear hiring motion and a newly opened role.

dimensions.label: Team Composition
dimensions.description: Founding team has strong engineering background, early engineers are visible from major tech or research contexts, and technical staff appear to be more than 60 percent of the team.

levels.0: Fully non-technical team building a technology product.
levels.1: Technical people are barely visible, or engineering appears outsourced.
levels.2: Team is mainly business development, operations, or consulting; technology appears auxiliary.
levels.3: Mixed team where technical people exist but do not clearly drive the company.
levels.4: Clear technical leader exists, with visible full-stack, infrastructure, or AI systems people.
levels.5: Founding team has strong engineering background, early engineers are visible from major tech or research contexts, and technical staff appear to be more than 60 percent of the team.

dimensions.label: Operating Model / Technical Closure
dimensions.description: Full technical closure around complex or innovative business problems: self-developed core systems, durable engineering assets, and evidence of owned data, model, training, fine-tuning, small-model, retrieval, workflow, runtime, eval, or infrastructure capability.

levels.0: Pure prompt studio, content mill, or third-party wrapper business.
levels.1: Short-cycle traffic product relying mostly on third-party models.
levels.2: Mainly custom implementation or delivery work, with productization far away.
levels.3: Consulting and product are mixed, with uncertain split.
levels.4: Strong in-house engineering and complex business context, but technical closure is incomplete or the model layer mainly depends on external platforms.
levels.5: Full technical closure around complex or innovative business problems: self-developed core systems, durable engineering assets, and evidence of owned data, model, training, fine-tuning, small-model, retrieval, workflow, runtime, eval, or infrastructure capability.

dimensions.label: Culture & Work Style
dimensions.description: Technical people have clear ownership and judgment rights, scope boundaries are explicit, and there is visible code review, quality bar, and technical debt awareness; pace is fast but sustainable.

levels.0: Exploitative, chaotic, or opaque environment with clearly irregular process or role boundaries.
levels.1: High agency appears to mean unlimited responsibility, low compensation pressure, or engineering subordinated to delivery; ownership and quality risks are high.
levels.2: Priorities are often pulled by sales or customer requests, product and engineering judgment appears weak, and technical scope is blurry.
levels.3: Ordinary startup culture or insufficient information; ownership, quality standards, and sustainable pace need more evidence.
levels.4: Technical voice is strong, builder culture is visible, and basic engineering quality standards exist; minor pace or boundary risks are controllable.
levels.5: Technical people have clear ownership and judgment rights, scope boundaries are explicit, and there is visible code review, quality bar, and technical debt awareness; pace is fast but sustainable.

dimensions.label: Technical Relevance
dimensions.description: Role core directly targets agent infra, retrieval, eval, runtime, memory, observability, AI/data systems, or production AI workflows.

levels.0: Does not build systems; mainly writes proposals, configuration, or operations delivery.
levels.1: Mainly demo building, prompt tuning, customer training, or lightweight prototyping.
levels.2: Mainly frontend, mobile, internal tools, or non-AI platform engineering.
levels.3: General backend or full-stack role, or the company has AI/data components but the role only partially touches them.
levels.4: Strongly related adjacent engineering: workflow automation, data integration, AI product infrastructure, observability, or full-stack AI product engineering.
levels.5: Role core directly targets agent infra, retrieval, eval, runtime, memory, observability, AI/data systems, or production AI workflows.

dimensions.label: Coding Ownership
dimensions.description: Long-term ownership of production code and system design, including maintenance, quality, review, and technical decisions.

levels.0: Engineer title but no real coding responsibility.
levels.1: Mainly customer communication, solutioning, project management, or delivery, with occasional scripts or demos.
levels.2: Mainly configuration, platform setup, low-code work, or data/workflow operations.
levels.3: Coding is explicitly part of the role, but the proportion, production path, or ownership boundary is unconfirmed.
levels.4: Coding is a major responsibility, with clear module or system ownership.
levels.5: Long-term ownership of production code and system design, including maintenance, quality, review, and technical decisions.

dimensions.label: Right to Work & Location
dimensions.description: Target location matches and the employer clearly can sponsor, or there is already a viable right-to-work path.

levels.0: Clearly cannot sponsor and there is no other right-to-work path; hard blocker.
levels.1: Employer clearly does not sponsor, but another personal route may exist.
levels.2: Feasibility is weak because it requires a new sponsor licence, cross-border remote conversion to employment, contract-to-perm, or another extra path.
levels.3: Location matches, but right-to-work or visa path is unconfirmed; no hard blocker, but it must be checked.
levels.4: Overall feasible, but location, employing entity, start date, or contract type needs handling.
levels.5: Target location matches and the employer clearly can sponsor, or there is already a viable right-to-work path.

dimensions.label: Interview Signal
dimensions.description: Process includes coding, system design, and a technical case or debugging exercise, so it can verify real engineering ability.

levels.0: Process clearly has no technical evaluation, or the process is abnormal or irregular.
levels.1: Process mainly tests communication, industry experience, or customer management.
levels.2: Process leans behavioral, consulting-style, or business-case-heavy, with light technical verification.
levels.3: Interview process is unknown; treat as neutral and record as missing information.
levels.4: Clear technical interview exists and includes coding, but the system design or case format is unconfirmed.
levels.5: Process includes coding, system design, and a technical case or debugging exercise, so it can verify real engineering ability.

decisionThresholds.label: Strong Fit
decisionThresholds.action: Prioritize: apply, find referral, customize materials.

decisionThresholds.label: Watch
decisionThresholds.action: Monitor hiring and funding; do not proactively apply.

decisionThresholds.label: Low Priority
decisionThresholds.action: Consider only if there are no better options.
